evidence.intree_statement: Definition sub_le (u v : SubObj x) : Type := { k : sub_dom u ~> sub_dom v & sub_mono v ∘ k ≈ sub_mono u }.  Lemma sub_le_refl (u : SubObj x) : sub_le u u.  Lemma sub_le_trans (u v w : SubObj x) : sub_le u v → sub_le v w → sub_le u w.

statement_record.book: For a topological space (X, Op), inclusion makes (Op, ⊆) a preorder — reflexive since U ⊆ U, transitive since U ⊆ V ⊆ W gives U ⊆ W — and hence, by the preorder-as-category passage of §3.2.3, a category Op whose objects are the open sets of X and whose hom-set Op(U,V) is empty when U ⊄ V and a singleton when U ⊆ V. This category is the site over which presheaves and sheaves on X are later defined.
statement_record.intree: Program Definition Proset {A : Type} {R : relation A} (P : PreOrder R) : Category := {| obj := A; hom := R; homset := fun A B => {| Setoid.equiv := fun _ _ => True |}; id := fun x => @reflexivity ... ; compose := fun x y z f g => @transitivity ... |}.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: only the GENERIC half is in force. Proset is exactly the passage the book invokes and is in fact more general than needed (any Type with a PreOrder, not just a subset order), and its trivial hom-setoid (equiv := fun _ _ => True) realizes thinness — 'at most one morphism', the hom being the proof of R x y — which matches the book's empty-or-singleton hom-set up to the usual proof-relevant/setoid rephrasing. What is missing is the SUBJECT: there is no topology, no set of opens, and hence no instantiation Proset (⊆ on Op). The closest in-tree inclusion-preorder is Theory/Subobject.v's factorization order on subobjects — sub_le_refl/sub_le_trans prove exactly 'the subobjects of an object form a preorder', which in Sets is the inclusion order on subsets — but it ranges over ALL subobjects, not over a distinguished family of opens, and it is never fed to Proset to produce a category.

gap: Missing: (a) topological spaces themselves (no topology/open-set structure anywhere in-tree — see def7.25), hence (b) no preorder (Op, ⊆) and no proof that inclusion of opens is reflexive and transitive (only the analogous sub_le_refl/sub_le_trans for subobjects), and (c) no resulting category Op(X) := Proset(⊆) and no Site instance on it (Theory/Sheaf.v's Class Site has NO instances in-tree), so the site over which Ch. 7's presheaves and sheaves are defined does not exist. Present: the generic preorder ⇒ thin category passage (Proset), with Poset adding antisymmetry.

statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the FRAMEWORK and one of the two recalled base cases are in force, the exercise's actual base is not. Enriched is exactly the V-category notion for an arbitrary monoidal base K, so 'V-category' is a real in-tree concept; and the recalled fact 'Bool-categories are preorders' is proven in-tree at full strength, as a two-way correspondence Enriched _2 ↔ TwoPreorder (both directions Defined), with the morphism leg EnrichedFunctor_Two_monotone (line 183) showing enriched functors are exactly the monotone maps. Two caveats on that direction: TwoPreorder carries an extra decidability field tpre_dec (needed to compute the hom truth value), and the base _2 is the walking arrow with its cartesian monoidal structure rather than a quantale in the book's sense (no joins are required of it). The exercise's own content — V = the quantale of opens — is unreachable: no topology, no Op, no quantale class exists (see remark7.33), so the enrichment base cannot be formed and no description of Op-categories is given anywhere. The other recalled base, Cost, is likewise prose-only: no [0,∞] enrichment base and no Lawvere metric space is built.

gap: Missing: (a) the base itself — the quantale V = (Op, ⊆, X, ∩) of a topological space cannot be constructed, since neither topologies/opens nor a quantale notion exist in-tree (see def7.25 and remark7.33); (b) consequently no instance @Enriched V of the enrichment class over such a V, and no description/characterization of what an Op-enriched category is (the intended answer: a set with, for each pair, the open subset of X on which x ≤ y holds); (c) the second recalled base case, Cost-categories = Lawvere metric spaces, is prose-only — no [0,∞] monoidal base is instantiated. Present: the general V-enrichment class (Enriched, with enriched functors), and the Bool case proven both ways (Enriched_Two_preorder, EnrichedFunctor_Two_monotone) plus V = Sets recovering ordinary categories (Category_is_Enriched_over_Set, Construction/Enriched.v:163).
